items.title: KI: Households worry more than normal
items.summary: The mood in the Swedish economy is largely unchanged in March, according to a barometer indicator from the Norwegian Economic Institute (KI). The indicator for the month rises slightly to 99.9, from 99.7 in February.
items.title_original: KI: Hushållen oroas mer än normalt
items.summary_original: Stämningsläget i svensk ekonomi är i stort sett oförändrat i mars, enligt en barometerindikator från Konjunkturinstitutet (KI). Indikatorn för månaden stiger svagt till 99,9, från 99,7 i februari.

items.title: New art gallery becomes a reality in Tornedalen: "It seemed completely crazy"
items.summary: What makes 1,500 private individuals, several wealthy enthusiasts and an art manager from Stockholm go in and support an art gallery in the middle of nowhere? The answer can be found in a village just south of the Arctic Circle, where the first sod has now been laid for Konsthall Tornedalen.
items.title_original: Ny konsthall blir verklighet i Tornedalen: ”Det verkade fullständigt skogstokigt”
items.summary_original: Vad får 1 500 privatpersoner, flera välbärgade entusiaster och en konstchef från Stockholm att gå in och stötta en konsthall mitt ute i ingenstans? Svaret finns i en by strax söder om polcirkeln, där det första spadtaget till Konsthall Tornedalen nu har tagits.

items.title: "Duty of information" will find more people in the shadow society
items.summary: The government and SD continue with the duty of information. Employees of a number of authorities must report to the police when they discover people who do not have the right to stay in Sweden.
items.summary_original: Regeringen och SD går vidare med informationsplikten. Anställda på ett antal myndigheter ska vara skyldiga att anmäla till polis när de upptäcker personer som inte har rätt att vistas i Sverige.

items.title: SEK 240 million in new support to Ukraine
items.summary: The Government has presented a new support package to Ukraine for 2026 worth around SEK 240 million. The support includes SEK 150 million for the Ukrainian Red Cross for humanitarian operations. In addition, the support package is heavily focused on children’s needs, supporting the provision of school food in areas close to the frontline, promoting reforms for family-based care of children and supporting children’s mental health.

items.title: SEK 555 million in new humanitarian aid for Gaza
items.summary: After more than two years of war and suffering, children in Gaza are in acute need of health and medical care, psychosocial support, safety, nutrition and education. Initiatives in these areas are needed to lay the foundations for reconstruction and recovery. Sweden is now providing SEK 555 million in aid, which will be distributed between the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF), the UN World Food Programme (WFP) and the United Nations Development Programme, and will help bring safety, stability and well-being to children in Gaza.

items.title: The policy rate remains unchanged at 1.75 percent
items.summary: The executive board has decided to leave the key interest rate unchanged at 1.75 percent and the interest rate is expected to remain at this level for some time to come. But the war in the Middle East makes the forecast very uncertain.  The Riksbank is following developments closely and will adapt monetary policy if the inflation and business cycle prospects require it.
items.summary_original: Direktionen har beslutat att lämna styrräntan oförändrad på 1,75 procent och räntan väntas ligga kvar på denna nivå under en tid framöver. Men kriget i Mellanöstern gör prognosen mycket osäker.  Riksbanken följer utvecklingen noga och kommer att anpassa penningpolitiken om inflations- och konjunkturutsikterna kräver det.

items.title: The Riksbank lowers the interest rate on the supplementary liquidity facility
items.summary: In the Riksbank's monetary policy control system, the interest rate that shall apply to the banks' overnight deposits and lending in the Riksbank is specified. In the Riksbank's supplementary liquidity facility, banks can take loans against collateral such as covered bonds. The interest surcharge on the supplementary liquidity facility is now reduced from 0.75 percentage points to 0.30 percentage points above the policy rate. In addition, the Riksbank removes the restriction on the percentage of covered bonds that the banks may use as collateral for loans from the Riksbank. The changes come into effect on 8 April 2026, and are part of the Riksbank's long-term work to facilitate banks' adaptation to an environment with less excess liquidity.
items.title_original: Riksbanken sänker räntan på den kompletterande likviditetsfaciliteten
items.summary_original: I Riksbankens penningpolitiska styrsystem anges vilken ränta som ska gälla för bankernas in- och utlåning över natten i Riksbanken. I Riksbankens kompletterande likviditetsfacilitet kan bankerna ta lån mot säkerheter som exempelvis säkerställda obligationer. Räntepåslaget på den kompletterande likviditetsfaciliteten sänks nu från 0,75 procentenheter till 0,30 procentenheter över styrräntan. Dessutom tar Riksbanken bort begränsningen för hur stor andel säkerställda obligationer bankerna får använda som säkerhet vid lån från Riksbanken. Förändringarna träder i kraft den 8 april 2026, och är en del av Riksbankens långsiktiga arbete med att underlätta bankernas anpassning till en miljö med mindre överskottslikviditet.

items.title: Sweden joins Pax Silica initiative
items.summary: On 17 March, Minister for Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard signed the Pax Silica Declaration in connection with her visit to Houston, Texas. The initiative brings together leading technology nations and aims to strengthen cooperation to secure supply chains for emerging technologies. Pax Silica will also help promote innovation, secure digital infrastructure and protect sensitive technologies.

items.title: Sweden provides humanitarian support to Lebanon
items.summary: Sweden is announcing a new SEK 65 million humanitarian aid package for Lebanon due to the ongoing military escalation between Israel and Hezbollah, which has caused a rapid deterioration in the humanitarian situation in the country. The support will be distributed among UN organisations, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and civil society to provide support and protection for people who now find themselves in the midst of the crisis.

items.title: The Payments Report 2026: Measures required to reduce vulnerability and increase inclusion in the payments market
items.summary: In order to reduce dependence on the outside world, the banks need to develop new payment services based on national and European systems. Primarily, banks must offer more services for instant payments, otherwise legislation should be introduced. To increase inclusion in the payment market, more payment methods are needed for those who do not have a payment account or experience digital exclusion. Access to cash services also needs to be improved, the Riksbank writes in the Payment Report published today.
items.title_original: Betalningsrapporten 2026: Åtgärder krävs för minskad sårbarhet och ökad inkludering på betalningsmarknaden
items.summary_original: För att minska omvärldsberoendet behöver bankerna utveckla nya betaltjänster som bygger på nationella och europeiska system. Primärt måste bankerna erbjuda fler tjänster för omedelbara betalningar, annars bör lagstiftning införas. För att öka inkluderingen på betalningsmarknaden behövs det fler betalsätt för de som saknar betalkonto eller upplever digitalt utanförskap. Tillgången till kontanttjänster behöver också förbättras, det skriver Riksbanken i Betalningsrapporten som publiceras idag.

items.title: The Riksbank's business survey: "It is not an obvious recovery, but we see that it is still happening"
items.summary: The large Swedish companies are experiencing a certain improvement in the economy, but the recovery is both slow and hesitant. The troubled global situation has noticeably affected household consumption and companies' willingness to invest, and makes companies cautious when looking ahead. This is shown by the Riksbank's company survey in February.
items.title_original: Riksbankens företagsundersökning: ”Det är ingen självklar återhämtning men vi ser att det ändå händer”
items.summary_original: De svenska storföretagen upplever en viss förbättring av konjunkturen, men återhämtningen är både långsam och tvekande. Det oroliga omvärldsläget har påverkat hushållens konsumtion och företagens investeringsvilja märkbart och gör företagen försiktiga när de blickar framåt. Det visar Riksbankens företagsundersökning i februari.
